items.desc:
Dans les hauts plateaux de Guji, à 2 200 mètres d’altitude, Tesfaye Bekele cultive un café qui porte en lui l’âme de l’Éthiopie. Fondateur de la ferme Suke Quto, il est l’une des figures emblématique de la filière éthiopienne; agronome, visionnaire et profondément engagé dans la régénération de son territoire.
La variété Kurume est ici travaillée en Honey : la cerise dépulpée sèche lentement avec son mucilage, conférant au café une douceur enveloppante et une complexité aromatique rare.
En tasse, une sucrosité de cassonade s’ouvre sur une acidité lumineuse aux accents d’ananas, avant une final

items.title: Gato Grande [Geisha Natural CRF #7]
items.desc:
Ce Geisha Naturel de Gato Grande est produit par Yessie Hartmann et Jean-Paul Langenstein, au coeur des Tierras Altas de Chiriquí, au Panama. Installée entre 1910 et 2000 mètres d’altitude, la ferme s’inscrit dans la continuité d’une longue histoire familiale : les Hartmann cultivent le café au Panama depuis plusieurs générations et ont largement contribué à la reconnaissance des cafés et surtout des Geishas panaméens.
Notre lot met en avant une lecture particulièrement élégante du Geisha en traitement Naturel. La dégustation s’ouvre sur une pomme fraîche et croquante, avant de laisser apparaî

items.title: Santa Elena [Geisha Pinnacle]
items.desc:
Cafelino est une entreprise familiale installée à Boquete, dans les montagnes de Chiriquí. Spécialisée dans le café de spécialité durable, elle allie tradition, innovation et respect de la nature pour offrir un café d’exception.
Au cœur de l’exploitation se trouve la Finca Santa Elena, perchée entre 1 250 et 1 530 mètres d’altitude. Grâce à son terroir volcanique unique et à des méthodes de production soignées, Santa Elena produit des cafés réputés pour leur arôme riche et leur qualité exceptionnelle.
Ce magnifique geisha est sublimé par le process exclusif Pinnacle, une méthode Hybrid d’une p

items.title: Janson [Los Alpes GN195]
items.desc:
Le Geisha naturel anaérobie 72h de Los Alpes Janson est un café qui révèle une expression plus intense et fruitée de cette variété mythique. Issu des parcelles de Volcan, dans la province de Chiriqui, ce Geisha illustre le savoir-faire de Janson dans la recherche d’une tasse à la fois expressive, précise et élégante.
Le process anaérobie de 72 heures vient ici amplifier naturellement la richesse aromatique du Geisha. En filtre, la tasse s’ouvre sur des notes d’hibiscus, florales et légèrement acidulées, qui donnent immédiatement beaucoup de fraîcheur et de vivacité. Le citron apporte ensuite u

items.title: Janson [Hacienda GW190]
items.desc:
Le Geisha Washed 190 (GW190) de la Hacienda Janson n’est pas un café qui cherche à impressionner par l’exubérance. Il séduit par sa clarté et l’expression de son terroir. Issu des parcelles de Volcan, dans la province de Chiriqui, ce Geisha illustre, comme toujours avec la café Janson, une lecture élégante de cette variété mytique.
Le process lavé agit ici comme un révélateur. il retire les artifices pour laisser parler la structure aromatique intrinsèque du Geisha. Le café en filtre évoque immédiatement un thé sencha fin, avec cette texture soyeuse et cette fraîcheur végétale caractéristique.

items.title: Hacienda la Esmeralda [Montana 3NC]
items.desc:
Un Geisha Naturel qui joue sur la finesse plutôt que sur la puissance, avec une tasse particulièrement expressive où le floral et le fruité se répondent avec beaucoup de précision.
Cultivé dans les hauteurs de Cañas Verdes, au sein de la mythique Hacienda La Esmeralda, ce Montaña 3NC est issu d’un micro-lot Geisha sélectionné pour son expression aromatique. Ici, le séchage naturel est travaillé afin de concentré les sucres du fruit tout en conservant la finesse et la transparence caractéristiques des Geishas de La Esmeralda.
En tasse, le jasmin apparaît dès les premières gorgées avec une fines

items.title: Calendrier de l’Avent
items.desc:
It’s that time of the year !
Cette année encore, TANAT vous propose un cadeau exceptionnel. Une sélection de 24 cafés de spécialité, réunis dans notre Calendrier de l’Avent 2026.
Une expérience unique réunissant les plus grands noms du café :
Hacienda La Esmeralda, Lost Origin, Elto, Finca Milan, Elida, Abu, Finca Deborah, Alo, et bien d’autres encore.
L’occasion rare de goûter des cafés venus des quatre coins du monde, dont certains lots spécialement dédiés à la compétition.
Un coffret d’exception célébrant la diversité et la richesse des cafés que nous proposons tout au long de l’année.
Chaq

items.title: Alo [Sky Project FL]
items.desc:
Issu du Sky Project d’Alo Coffee, ce lot pousse dans le village d’Alo, à Bensa. L’idée du projet est aussi simple que radicale : aller chercher des altitudes où les nuits plus fraîches ralentissent la maturation des cerises. Une maturation plus lente permet aux fruits d’accumuler davantage de sucres et de développer une expression aromatique particulièrement dense.
En tasse, le café joue sur la carte du fruit et de la fraîcheur. La pêche apparaît d’abord : pulpeuse, mûre, juteuse. Puis arrive le raisin rouge et sa sucrosité éclatante. Enfin, se dévoile la groseille avec son acidité vive.

items.title: Finca Rosma [Geisha Washed]
items.desc:
Un Geisha lavé tout en finesse, issu de la Finca Rosma à Huehuetenango. Cette ferme familiale, fondée en 1963 par Alejandro Morales est aujourd’hui dirigée par la famille Morales.
La tasse s’ouvrira sur des notes délicates de jasmin et de citron, amenant une acidité élégante. Puis, le café gagnera en douceur, des notes d’abricot sucrés accompagnées d’une texture soyeuse évoquant le lait d’amande. Un café équilibré, floral et lumineux.

items.title: Granja Paraiso 92 [Red Bourbon Advanced Washed]
items.desc:
Un espresso colombien signé Wilton Benitez, issu de la mythique Granja Paraiso 92, dans la Valle Del Cauca. Ici, le red bourbon est travaillé avec une approche expérimentale, notamment avec la fermentation contrôlée lavée qui vient pousser l’expression aromatique tout en conservant en tasse un équilibre net et précis.
En espresso, le profil s’ouvre sur une violette très expressive, puis laisse apparaître une sensation de liqueur de cerises, dense et légèrement acidulée, avant de s’étirer sur un chocolat noir plus profond. Une tasse à la fois florale, liquoreuse et structurée, où la fermentatio

items.title: Alo [Zero Fermentation Washed]
items.desc:
Derrière ce Zero Fermentation Washed, Alo cherche à retirer une étape devenue presque incontournable dans les lavés modernes : la fermentation. Les cerises mûres sont triées, dépulpées puis lavées immédiatement, sans passage en cuves. L’objectif, simple en apparence est très exigeant en pratique, il faut éviter que la fermentation ne façonne le profil aromatique et laisser la variété et le terroir s’exprimer avec le moins d’interférences possibles.
La tasse s’ouvre sur une texture aérienne, avec une première note de thé blanc qui se dévoile dans le palais. Vient alors la cerise, fraîche et aci

items.title: Elto [Elora RF8 Natural]
items.desc:
Au coeur du projet Elto Coffee, la fermentation tient un rôle de véritable levier d’expression du terroir.
Pour notre lot RF8 Naturel, les cerises fermentent naturellement dans des sacs hermétiques immergés dans une rivière, avant un séchage lent permettant de préserver la richesse aromatique développée pendant le processus.
En tasse, le café donne une sensation de douceur. La cerise vient apporter une sucrosité fruitée et éclatante ; vite suivie par la rose séchée, la tasse prend une dimension florale, délicate et parfumée. Enfin, le bubblegum prolonge la douceur dans la gourmandise, voire ve

items.title: Santa Elena [Geisha Aura]
items.desc:
Cultivé à la Santa Elena, sur les pentes du Cerro Piedra de Lino au coeur de la vallée de Boquete, ce Geisha profite d’un terroir particulièrement favorable à l’expression aromatique de la variété. C’est entre 1200 et 1550 mètres d’altitude que la ferme cultive différentes variétés d’arabica, dont le Geisha. Santa Elena est aujourd’hui porté par la famille Ameglio, dont l’histoire agricole au Panama remonte à plusieurs générations. La ferme a été acquise en 2011 par Marco et Xenia Ameglio, qui ont depuis entrepris de moderniser progressivement la plantation et leurs méthodes de production.

items.title: Jamison Savage [Caturra Washed]
items.desc:
Le Panama ne produit simplement de superbes Geishas, parce que au milieu de cette obsession pour les tasses emplie de clarté et de pureté, il existe des cafés beaucoup plus directs, plus gourmands, tout en restant équilibrés. Ce Caturra Lavé de Jamison Savage en fait partie.
La tasse commence sur quelque chose de gourmand : le chocolat au lait, puis arrive la prune rouge, avec cette sensation vive et élégante que l’on retrouve dans les cafés kenyans. Enfin, ces notes s’élargissent vers la noisette, en laissant une sensation douce et généreuse en bouche. Un Caturra qui ne cherche pas à jouer au

items.title: Los Lajones Porton [GN #23109]
items.desc: Notre lot Geisha Naturel 23109 provient de Los Lajones, la ferme de Graciano Cruz, dans la région de Boquete au Panama. La propriété en elle-même est très très intéressante. Une grande partie de son territoire reste couverte de forêt, et les plantations de café occupent notamment les secteurs plus élévés. Graciano Cruz a une approche construite autour des procédés classiques de traitement, avec une volonté de travailler le café sans chercher à le rendre artificiellement spectaculaire. Le principe est plutôt de donner au fruit et à la variété suffisamment de temps pour exprimer ce qu’ils ont a

items.title: Hacienda la Esmeralda [Lino 6HC]
items.desc:
Cultivé à haute altitude dans la région de Boquete, au Panama, au sein de la célèbre Hacienda la Esmeralda, le café Lino 6HC bénéficie d’un procédé honey avec séchage contrôlé, où le séchage des cerises avec une partie de mucilage est maîtrisé afin de préserver la complexité aromatique tout en développant douceur et profondeur. Le nom Lino ne désigne pas une variété, mais un bien lot spécifique de la ferme, en isolant des parcelles précises, Hacienda la Esmeralda vient chercher à isoler les expressions les plus intéressantes du terroir.
Notre lot Lino 6HC de Hacienda la Esmeralda est donc une

items.title: Finca Sophia [RW4 – Colibri-Poro 40 GW] – Auction Lot
items.desc:
L’équipe de Tanat Coffee est honorée de partager avec vous deux lots obtenus lors de la vente aux enchères de la Finca Sophia. Deux cafés Geisha lavés exceptionnels, qui témoignent de notre admiration pour l’engagement, la rigueur et la passion de l’équipe Finca Sophia.
Ces deux lots lavés vous feront découvrir deux profils sensoriels authentiques, mettant en valeur la pureté de la variété, le soin apporté à son terroir ainsi que la maîtrise d’un procédé de lavage d’une extrême précision.
Une acidité d’agrumes douce et vive ouvre sur des notes de mandarine, de nectarine, de bonbon au citron et

items.title: Elto [Hamasho 96h]
items.desc:
Sur les hauts plateaux de Bensa, en Éthiopie, se trouve Elto Coffee, projet d’Eliyas Dukamo et d’Atiklit Dejene. Forts tous deux d’une solide expérience dans la production de cafés d’exception en Éthiopie, ils ont créé Elto Coffee avec l’ambition de repousser les standards de qualité en mettant la lumière les terroirs de Bensa et des méthodes de lavage plus modernes.
Sur notre lot Elto Hamasho, les 96 heures de fermentation construisent une tasse d’une intensité forte, mais toujours lisible. En début de dégustation, les fruits noirs prennent la main, une myrtille juteuse, une mûre éclatante, u

items.title: Alo [Digs Project Anaerobic Honey 48h]
items.desc:
Direction les hauts plateaux de Bensa, au coeur du village d’Alo, où le producteur Tamiru Tadesse signe des cafés parmi les plus recherché d’Éthiopie. Ce lot est issu d’une fermentation anaérobie honey avec 48h de fermentation. Les cerises sont sélectionnées minutieusement avant de fermenter en environnement anaérobie pendant deux jours, permettant un développement aromatique intense ; après cette fermentation contrôlée, le café est dépulpé puis séché lentement sur lits africains, avec une partie du mucilage préservée pour apporter d’avantage de sucrosité.
Ce café est produit dans le cadre du

items.title: Gesha Village [Oma Anaerobic Natural 26/E24]
items.desc:
Issu de mythique terroir de Gesha Village, au coeur de la région de West Omo en Éthiopie, ce lot Oma G26 E24 est cultivé sur les pentes du bloc Oma, où la variété Gesha 1931 exprime tpute sa finesse. La fermentation en anaérobie naturelle de ce lot apporte une profondeur aromatique remarquable sans masquer l’identité du terroir.
En tasse, l’ouverture est aérienne. Le coquelicot vient évoquer une douceur florale, rejoint par une myrtille juteuse et l’orange vient ensuite illuminer l’ensemble d’une fraîcheur vive, laissant une finale longue et élégante.
Chaque tasse évoluera en refroidissant, dé

items.title: Janson [Hacienda GW121]
items.desc:
Découvrez ce magnifique lot 121 Geisha lavé issue de la plantation Hacienda Janson. Il se dévoilera en tasse un café expressif et pur, caractéristique des hauts plateaux de la région de Chiriqui, au Panama, nichée sur les hauts plateaux de Volcan.
Un café d’une grande douceur et élégance, sa texture soyeuse, sa finesse florale rappelant le chèvrefeuille et sa finale longue abricot en font un grand cru d’exception.

items.title: Alo Bore [Washed]
items.desc:
Ce lot vient des hauteurs du Guji, en Éthiopie, où Tamiru Tadesse cultive la variété 74158 à plus de 2000 mètres d’altitude.
Traité en lavé, il offre une tasse nette et florale, où les fleurs blanches laissent place à la pêche, avant une finale vive de pamplemousse.

items.title: Choco Nuts
items.desc: Choco Nuts is our latest Brazilian espresso, produced by Adriano Muñiz and his family at Agropecuária Muñiz in Sul de Minas. This anaerobic natural Catucaí has everything we enjoy in a classic Brazilian coffee, with plenty of sweetness, a round body and a creamy texture. Expect notes of hazelnut, milk chocolate and vanilla, making it a great everyday espresso that also works really well with milk.

items.title: Pillow Talk
items.desc: Los Nogales does decaf a little differently. This Caturra is grown, processed and decaffeinated at the farm in Pitalito, giving Oscar Hernandez and his team control over the coffee from cherry to finished decaf. It’s bright and sweet, with starfruit, agave and rosemary. A decaf we’d happily drink whether we were looking for one or not. * Due to the decaffeination process, the beans may have an unusual colour. This is completely normal and does not affect the quality of the coffee.

items.title: Peachy Daze
items.desc: Peachy Daze is back, a clean washed Ethiopian from the Chelbesa washing station in Gedeb, where heirloom varieties grow at 2173 masl. The cup is light and delicate, with white peach and lemon up front, black tea through the middle and a soft elderflower finish.

items.title: Blackberry Dust
items.desc: Blackberry Dust is a late-harvest natural Ethiopian coffee from the Buku Abel washing station in Guji, which arrived in Europe just a few weeks ago. Around 400 smallholder farmers contribute to the station, growing heirloom varieties at elevations between 1,900 and 2,100 masl. The cup is fruity and sweet, with notes of blackberry, wild strawberry and blueberry yoghurt, followed by a soft, creamy finish.

items.title: Macaron
items.desc: One of our all-time favourites from Johan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, this natural Red Bourbon has become one of those coffees we’re always excited to bring back. It goes through an advanced anaerobic natural process and comes out big, juicy and seriously sweet, with strawberry jam, raspberry macaron and buttercream.

items.title: Sticky Pudding
items.desc: Our Christmas coffee is here! This year we’ve worked with CATA Export in Colombia to create something inspired by the festive season. This bourbon undergoes a co-fermentation with cinnamon, cardamom, mandarin and cherry, giving it a distinctive profile while keeping plenty of sweetness in the cup. Expect notes of cinnamon, cardamom and fresh fir – a very festive profile.

items.title: Cream Donut
items.desc: Cream Donut is a collaboration with Cata Export and producer Franky Hoyos in Colombia. A yeast-inoculated natural Caturra Chiroso developed for DAK through rounds of back-and-forth trialling. It’s an unusual coffee that has somehow become one of our staples and a bestseller, loved for its distinct character and the ridiculously good flat white it makes. Expect chocolate milk, cherry-filled doughnut and vanilla, whether you brew it as filter or espresso.

items.title: Milky Cake
items.desc: Milky Cake has been with us since 2021 and has become one of our bestsellers. Originally developed with Cata Export and Diego Samuel Bermudez at Finca El Paraíso in Colombia, it’s an advanced anaerobic washed Castillo with a profile that’s hard to mistake for anything else. Vanilla cake, pistachio, cardamom and honey, with a creamy sweetness that works as filter, espresso or with milk.

items.title: Plum Butter
items.desc: Plum Butter is a natural from Bulambuli in East Uganda, produced with our long-time partners at Ibero. It’s a profile we don’t come across often from Uganda: deep, smooth and fruit-forward, with dark plum, grape cordial and cacao. Rich without becoming too heavy.

items.title: Berry Blues
items.desc: Berry Blues is back. We’ve had this coffee in different variations over the years, sometimes under Berry Blues, sometimes as Blueberry Boom, and it remains a favourite across the DAK team for its big fruit character and how much fun it is to drink. This year’s harvest from Esayas Beriso is an anaerobic natural, grown high in Oromia, Ethiopia, and slowly dried in the shade. There’s plenty of dark fruit and a boozy edge: grape soda up front, myrtle liquor behind it, and a cashew-butter richness that gives the cup its buttery body and creamy mouthfeel.

items.title: Darling
items.desc: Darling comes from Danche Washing Station in Gedeb, and it’s one of the more delicate Ethiopians we’ve had this year. The coffee goes through a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation before being washed, resulting in a cup with good clarity despite the additional fermentation. Wild florals lead, followed by peach iced tea and a black-tea finish. Light, elegant and very tea-like.

items.title: Rhubarb Fizz
items.desc: Our next Kenyan of the season, and one of our favourites this year. Rhubarb Fizz is a washed AA from Ndimi Factory in Kirinyaga, bringing together SL28, SL34, Batian and Ruiru 11 from the surrounding smallholder farms. Juicy and layered, with rhubarb soda, blackcurrant and orange.

items.title: Hazel Nuts
items.desc: Hazel Nuts is a natural Catuaí from Chinacla in the Marcala region of Honduras, grown by our longtime partners Marysabel Caballero and Moises Herrera. We’ve been buying their coffees for years, and this is one we particularly like for espresso. Round and silky, with hazelnut, cacao nibs and blackberry, plus a touch of booziness that we really enjoy. Especially good with milk.

items.title: Silky Way
items.desc: Silky Way is another coffee from Jhoan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, the same family behind Macaron. This time it’s their washed Pink Bourbon, with a completely different side of the farm showing up in the cup. Lemongrass, white florals and crisp green apple, with a bright, sparkling quality that suits the name pretty well.

items.title: The Alchemist
items.desc: The Alchemist is one of the staples in our line-up and a coffee we source directly from Gasharu Farms in Nyamasheke, Rwanda. An anaerobic natural Red Bourbon that changes quite a bit depending on how you brew it. Espresso pushes the cacao forward; filter opens up the tropical fruit and jammy sweetness. Complex, rich and particularly good with milk.

items.title: Jazz fruits
items.desc: Jazz Fruits is a staple in our lineup and one we try to keep around all year, whenever the harvest allows. We source this community lot from Daye Bensa each year for its fruity, easy-going profile and how well it works as espresso, especially with milk. Strawberry, white chocolate and mandarin in the cup. Named after the Jazz Fruits playlists on Spotify.

items.title: Mucho Berry Blend
items.desc:
Mucho Berry
Momos Coffee’s fourth signature blend
Ethiopia is widely known as one of the coffee-growing regions loved by many people. In particular, Ethiopian coffees processed by the natural method are recognized for their diverse berry-like aromas and their broad appeal, making them enjoyable for a wide range of drinkers.
Inspired by these berry characteristics, the fourth signature blend, Mucho Berry, was created to express rich and attractive berry-forward aromas.

items.title: Fruity Bonbon Blend
items.desc:
Fruity Bonbon
Momos Coffee’s second signature blend
In 2009, when specialty coffee was first encountered in the United States, coffees with bright acidity and fruit-like aromas were still unfamiliar to many people. However, drawn to the diverse aromas and new flavors found in high-quality coffee, Momos Coffee introduced its second signature blend, Fruity Bonbon, to share the distinct character and appeal of specialty coffee.

items.title: Es Chocolat Blend
items.desc:
Es Chocolat
Momos Coffee’s first signature blend
Es Chocolat, the very first signature blend introduced by Momos Coffee, was developed at a time when dark-roasted coffees reminiscent of chocolate were the mainstream style. It reflects the early days of Momos Coffee and the intention to create a coffee that could be enjoyed and loved by everyone.

This ultra limited coffee came direct from Diego Bermudez as part of his Hachi project, and this is certainly one of the more uniquely processed coffees we've ever offered, all while maintaining clean, lush fruit flavors. This coffee is ripe and big with cranberry and tart cherry flavors, along with crushed pineapple and glimmering caramel notes.

items.desc:
Fresh Colombian geshas are bursting onto the scene, and this latest addition is a knockout. Diamond Reserve gesha brings cherry & apricot flavor combined with the tropical charm of guava. We also tasted peach, berries, and the depth of caramel. This went to our monthly subscribers last month, and we have a handful of bags rested & ready to drink from that date!

items.desc:
Welcome back Perlitas! This is our second edition of Perlitas Chiroso and we are excited to share it with you. Usually Perlitas is a combo of caturra, pink bourbon, etc, but Stephen from The Coffee Quest sent us this pure chiroso version and we loved it. The Chiroso variety is expanding rapidly in Colombia, and we're excited to bring in even more as new trees mature. Renowned for its flavor quality, this relative of Ethiopian landrace varieties is a beautiful, clean coffee with flavors of orange, currant, and a warm spice reminiscent of clove. Also available green!

items.desc:
As we say goodbye to our Zuria Blend, we present the all new Alpenglow, Prodigal's limited fall blend. The washed Ethiopian brings ripe fruits, the chiroso brings the balance and warmth, and the glamorous gesha adds notable depth and complexity. The flavors are dazzling pineapple, pulpy, ripe orange, and tart cranberry. This coffee has no business being this good, and we loved formulating it for you!

items.title: Gesha Harmony
items.desc:

Fabiola's daughter Marilin Muñoz produced this coffee, and its ripe peach, grape, and cola flavors are a knockout. We also tasted cranberry, jasmine, and syrupy apricot. Scott brewed a stash of this coffee in Panama at the World of Coffee event, and the reception was wonderful. Our October subscribers received this coffee first, but we couldn't hold it back for long, so now it's available for everyone!

items.desc:
With great joy and sadness we are announcing this final Honduran coffee of 2026, and it is tremendous. Angel Arturo Paz set aside a tiny bit of his special Dark Room Dried (DRD) geisha for us, and we are supremely honored. This coffee is ripe and saturated, with exotic yet refined flavors. We've never put "watermelon" as a tasting note on a Prodigal release before, but this coffee has earned its pedigree. With huge pineapple, red wine, and watermelon, this is truly a special coffee. We also tasted grape jelly, strawberry, rhubarb, and a lovely, tart acidity.

items.desc:

The flavors are layered orange and tart cherry, with even a hint of pineapple, grape, and raspberry. The aromas are rose and powdered sugary blueberries. This is classic, washed Ethiopian coffee.
This coffee is named for the Danche washing station where it's produced. Approximately 800 farmers deliver their coffee cherries to this washing station, each farming 2-3 hectares of land at 2200 meters.

This is a super fun coffee, combining everything we love about classic Ethiopian flavors. Look for citrus and florals from the washed component and rich cherry flavor from the natural. Mulu is punchy and ripe and makes great straight espresso and americanos.

items.title: Decaf Beans
items.desc:
A quality washed Red Bourbon from Rwanda. It has preserved the pleasant stewed fruit and spice notes associated with Rwandan coffee.
This is the first time we have launched a Rwandan decaffeinated coffee. Like the Ethiopian decaf that we launched earlier this year, this coffee nicely displays the character of its origin.

items.title: SOLO
items.desc:
SOLO is a seasonal single-origin washed coffee offering a molasses sweetness, gentle berry acidity and a syrupy body that carries through to a great finish.
In the highlands of western Guatemala, smallholder producers in Huehuetenango farm steep, fertile slopes where coffee sustains much of the local economy. Working collectively through the Regional Select programme, they’ve built a system that rewards quality while keeping value close to origin. This lot was crafted to capture the essence of Huehuetenango's flavour.

items.title: Foundation Beans
items.desc:
A great example of Costa Rican coffee offering rounded sweetness, mellow acidity and a full mouthfeel.
This coffee is brought to us by Cafe Imports, whose sourcing programme in Costa Rica is centred around Oxcart Coffee, their local import-export operation. Oxcart aims to work with the same micromills year after year, building lasting relationships. Beyond its commercial role, Oxcart also acts as a resource for the local coffee community by promoting candid conversations about quality and production. items.title: Rare Beans

Gara Agena sits on a steep hillside at approximately 2,250 MASL, with the Geta River wrapping around the site. This location was not chosen by accident: it offers ideal elevation, growing conditions and access to clean water. The site is overseen by Mr Faysel A. Yonis, the owner of Testi Coffee. items.title: Gesha Beans
items.desc:

Yulisa Carhuallocllo Arévalo grew up learning about coffee in El Corazón, a small community in Peru’s northern Cajamarca region. Her father, Efraín Carhuallocllo Salvador, began planting his farm “El Cerro” in 2005, gradually expanding his Caturra plots with training and technical support from the Cenfrocafé cooperative. In 2017, his coffee placed second at Peru’s first Cup of Excellence. Yulisa gained valuable experience in both production and the assessment of quality by working with her father.

items.title: Familia Toledo Ortiz - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This lot comes from the combined harvests of father-and-son producers Edernoman Toledo Charry and Yoan Arley Toledo, who shared this coffee with us under their family name, Toledo Ortiz. Both Edernoman and Yoan were responsible for some of our favorite coffees of 2026, and we’re excited to be closing out the year with an outstanding pink bourbon variety separation that they produced together on their family farm, Finca Los Andes. As two of the most exciting talents to emerge from our longstanding Divino Niño partnership in recent years, we can’t wait to see what the future holds for these two.

items.title: La Tortuga - Washed Process - Education Lot - 2025
items.desc: After a brief hiatus, we're delighted to welcome back La Tortuga, one of Passenger’s original Education Lot menu favorites. This community blend, produced by an association of small coffee farmers on the Galápagos Islands, offers a fascinating example of the impact of unique microclimates on specialty coffee production. While produced at elevations far below what is typically considered appropriate for specialty coffee production, this coffee defies expectations thanks to the fortuitous environmental impact of the Humboldt Current. In the cup, we find aromatics of marzipan and browning sugar,

items.title: William Abad - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: This mejorado variety separation comes from producer William Abad’s farm, El Pino, located in Ecuador’s Zamora region. While most of our sourcing in Ecuador has focused on the Pichincha region in the north-central part of the country, we’ve occasionally featured exceptional producers from Zamora as well. Zamora is located nearly three hundred miles southeast of the Pichincha region near the Amazon basin, and close to neighboring Peru. The area's proximity to the Amazon rainforest creates a more humid and tropical environment compared to the mountainous terrain of Pichincha, perhaps contributin

items.title: Finca Perla Negra - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Perla Negra is an award-winning farm in Pichincha, Ecuador, run by Olger Rogel and Magda Zabala alongside their daughter, Nanci Rogel. Known for their exploration of unconventional coffee genetics, the family grows a diverse collection of varieties and unique selections. This particular lot is composed of a variety that Olger calls ‘Lupe Maria.’ Although its provenance has yet to be confirmed through genetic testing, its morphology bears some resemblance to Coffea eugenioides , a species also cultivated on the farm and one of the ancestral species of Arabica. items.title: Silvio Leite - Natural Process - 2023
items.desc: Benefiting from its proximity to the Chapada Diamantina mountain range, the Piatã municipality in Brazil’s Bahia region is home to some of the most celebrated coffees in the country. This dry processed lot from legendary producer Silvio Leite in Piatã was awarded second place among a collection of his auction lot coffees from the 2022 harvest year. Kept in freezer preservation since it's arrival to our warehouse in early 2023, we're delighted to share the very last of this Reserve Lot as one last archival release for the year. We've been finding nuanced aromatics of floral honey and orange pee

items.title: 2026 Holiday Coffee & Herbal Blend
items.desc: Why choose between coffee and tea? The more the merrier is what we say! This bundle features a 250 gram bag of Holiday Coffee and a 50 gram tube of Holiday Herbal.

items.title: Holiday Coffee - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This year’s Holiday Coffee features a selection from our newest Foundational Partnership, Thamani, in Kenya. This washed Kamathura lot, sourced through our partners at Kamavindi Coffee Labs, brings together coffees from two distinct cooperative societies: Gichathaini Factory and Murarandia Factory. In the cup, we find a festive array of seasonal flavors, including notes of spiced plum and cranberry complemented by bright orange zest and a comforting chocolate finish.

items.title: Necessary Holiday Blend 2026
items.desc: This rich and comforting blend has balanced notes of warming spices, toffee, and dark chocolate, making it the perfect cup for sharing with loved ones, fueling traditions old and new, and enjoying all throughout the season.

items.title: Kerehaklu Peaberry - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This peaberry lot comes from a small selection of early outturns from the 2025–26 harvest at Kerehaklu Estate. The Selection 9 variety featured in this lot ripens earlier than many of the other varieties common to the area, and the small size of peaberries requires specialized milling equipment. As a result, Pranoy chose to mill these lots separately and earlier in the harvest cycle. Many of these peaberry lots remained in-country, finding their way onto the menus of some of India’s most celebrated specialty roasters. When we visited Kerehaklu earlier this year, however, Pranoy mentioned a sep

items.title: Kerehaklu - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This selection from the 2025–26 harvest at Kerehaklu Estate in Chikmagalur, India, features what producer Pranoy Thipiah describes as an Extended Mosto Washed process. It begins with the creation of a ‘mosto,’ made from a mix of parchment coffee and coffee cherry mucilage that creates a starter culture from the active native yeasts and bacteria present on the remaining fruit. items.title: Kerehaklu - Natural Process - 2026
items.desc: When producer Pranoy Thipiah invited us into his quality lab outside Kerehaklu Estate's processing site earlier this year, we couldn’t help but notice something intriguing: a small, lidded barrel filled with whole coffee cherries and a pink-hued liquid, with an aquarium bubbler slowly adding oxygen to the mixture. As it turns out, this small experiment would lead to a massive cup profile when scaled up. It's what Pranoy calls his Oxygenated Cascara Mosto Natural. items.title: Thamani
items.desc: The most recent addition to the Foundational Menu, this vibrant field blend features the renowned SL28 and SL34 varieties. While Thamani may be sourced from other producer partners in the years to come, this inaugural expression was produced at Kamavindi Estate by our dear friends the Mbature family.

items.title: Kambarare - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc:
Last year marked our first time purchasing coffee from Gerald Njagi, a third generation coffee producer and manager of Kambarare Estate in Kirinyaga County in Kenya.
Through continued collaboration with the Mbature family and their export operations at Kamavindi Coffee Lab, we are delighted to be able to feature another outstanding washed SL variety lot from the most recent harvest at Kambarare. Again this year, the quality of Gerald's single variety SL separations stood out on the cupping table for their refined flavor complexity, and notable depth of sweetness. This particular lot of SL vari

items.title: Bumba - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: This Reserve Lot selection is one of two coffees in our most recent release featuring lots processed at the Long Miles Ninga washing station. Run by meticulous station manager Agathon Ininahazwe, Ninga station is capable of producing extraordinary washed and honey-processed coffees. This particular washed lot is made up of small harvests from producers from nearby Bumba hill in Kayanza province. A classic Burundi profile, we’re tasting dark dried fruit and breakfast tea in the cup, alongside mild orange acidity and spiced chocolate in the finish.

items.title: Luz Mary Hurtado - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Luz Mary Hurtado is one of a growing number of award-winning coffee producers we've had the privilege of discovering through our long-standing Divino Niño partnership in the municipality of Suaza in Central Huila. Last fall, Luz placed among the top twenty producers in the Central Region category of the annual Copa de Oro competition, and her exceptional talent is once again on display in this impressively sweet and nuanced field blend of pink bourbon and gesha varieties. A fitting expression of the plant genetics at play, we taste classic pink bourbon characteristics of sweet dark berries and

items.title: Abdo Aba Mecha - EA Decaf - Education Lot - 2025
items.desc: This decaf Education Lot is a blend of washed and natural processed lots from the 30 hectare estate of producer Abdo Aba Mecha. Abdo began working with our import partners at Osito back in 2023, around the same time that we featured a natural processed lot from one of Abdo’s neighbors, Nesru Abanura. This area, in Ethiopia’s western Jimma Zone, is close to many of of the producers we work closely with for our Agaro Foundational partnership, so we’ve been delighted to see it continue to develop as a hub for talented, quality-driven producers. We selected this lot as a candidate for the Educatio

items.title: Fausto Romo Sidra - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Released alongside a honey processed lot from the 2025 harvest at La Carolina in Pichincha, Ecuador, this washed processed sidra variety separation from producer Fausto Romo exemplifies why sidra has become synonymous with specialty coffees from Ecuador. In the cup we taste vibrant white grape, subtle florals, and an integrated panela-like sweetness, followed by a finish of soft pome fruit reminiscent of pear and yellow apple.

items.title: Wilmer Julca - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Now in our second consecutive year working with producer Wilmer Julca, this selection from his 2025 harvest exemplifies the outstanding quality potential of coffees grown at extremely high elevations in the celebrated coffee producing region of Cajamarca, Peru. In the cup we find a deeply sweet and savory quality reminiscent of molasses, cooked fruit, and spiced orange.

items.title: Abel Raymundo Arotaype - Washed Process - Cup of Excellence - 2024
items.desc: It’s no exaggeration to say that the Abel Raymundo Arotaype Huayllas is among the highest elevation coffee producers in the world. Located at nearly 2500 masl, his farm, El Pedregal, is located in the west of Cusco near the border with the neighboring Ayacucho department. This past year we’ve tasted a number of outstanding geshas from this region, so it was no surprise to see this coffee given due acclaim at the 2024 Peru Cup of Excellence, where it was awarded 11th place overall.

items.title: Familia Morales Rivera - Washed Process - Cup of Excellence - 2022
items.desc: Carefully preserved since arriving at our freezer facility in the spring of 2023, this coffee continues to be among the highest-scoring coffees ever to come across Passenger’s cupping table. Simply put, its cup profile possesses a level of refinement and complexity that we rarely encounter from coffees anywhere in the world. Awarded third place in the 2022 Ecuador Cup of Excellence competition, it's an immaculate expression of the Sidra and Mejorado varieties from the Rivera family farm in Pichincha, Ecuador, providing a glimpse into the extraordinary potential of Ecuador’s signature plant gen

items.title: Daterra Aramosa - Natural - Education Lot - 2024
items.desc: The Aramosa ‘pre-cultivar’ featured in this Education Lot is the result of a unique hybridization between two distinct species of the Coffea genus: Arabica and Racemosa. The result is a more drought tolerant and pest resistant plant that exhibits a vibrant cup character and a naturally lower-caffeine content. As with the majority of the natural process lots from Daterra, cherries for this lot were ‘dried on tree’ before being harvested and sorted. This cup has many of the fruit-forward flavors we’ve come to expect from these unique plant genetics: Plum and fruit taffy flavors with an herbal fl

items.title: Daterra Catuai SH3 - Natural - Education Lot - 2024
items.desc: The catuai SH3 cultivar featured in this Education Lot selection from Daterra offers a case study in how coffee producers and research institutions around the world are working together to combat the effects of climate change on coffee production through careful study of coffee plant genetics and the development of new more climate resilient varieties. As with the majority of the natural process lots from Daterra, cherries for this lot were fully ‘dried on tree’ before being harvested and sorted. In the cup we find a notable Meyer lemon acidity, balanced by flavors of praline and dark chocolat

items.title: Necessary India
items.desc: A bold, grounding blend of arabica and robusta from Passenger’s Bhadra partnership. This coffee brings together rich notes of dark chocolate and toasted sesame, with a smooth intensity that’s perfect for everyday drinking.

items.title: Bhadra
items.desc: This delightfully sweet and approachable coffee comes from a small group of family-run coffee farms that together make up the Bhadra partnership. All of these estates are located near the Bhadra Tiger Reserve, in the historically significant coffee-growing region of Chikmagalur, India.

items.title: Necessary Decaf
items.desc: The rich, malted chocolate and maple syrup qualities of this incredibly sweet decaffeinated coffee from Colombia prove that no decaf drinker should ever need to compromise on flavor.

items.title: Los Sueños - Decaf
items.desc: Our Los Sueños Decaf is comprised of community lots from our producer partners in Divino Niño. These lots are Ethyl Acetate decaffeinated in Colombia before heading directly to our freezer storage facility in Lancaster.

items.title: Stowaway
items.desc: Comprised of coffees from three Foundational Partnerships, Montecarlos, Agaro, and Cusco, Stowaway is an incredibly balanced and widely approachable blend that has served as the mainstay espresso offering at Passenger's flagship King St. café in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, since our beginnings.

items.title: Divino Niño
items.desc: Centrally located in the celebrated producing region of Huila, producers near the small hamlet of Divino Niño produce this outstanding community blend that exemplifies the hallmark flavors of a classic Colombian coffee.

items.title: Necessary Dark
items.desc: With comforting flavors of bittersweet chocolate and graham cracker, this classic Dark Roast tastes great on its own or with the addition of cream and sugar.

items.title: Necessary Ethiopia
items.desc: The hallmark qualities of Ethiopian coffee abound in this refreshing and balanced cup, with flavors of stone fruit, florals, and a sweet toffee-like finish.

items.title: Necessary Burundi
items.desc: Dark berries, subtle warming spices, and a molasses-like sweetness come together in this quintessential Burundi selection.

items.title: Heza
items.desc: Highlighting the exceptional work of the Long Miles Coffee Project, the complex and unique flavor profile of Burundian coffee is on full display in this Foundational offering comprised of coffees processed at the Heza washing station.

items.title: Montecarlos
items.desc: This rich and inviting Foundational offering comes from visionary fifth-generation coffee producer Carlos Batres and his wife Julie, who have remained steadfast and pioneering stewards of the Montecarlos Estate since the 1980's

items.title: Cusco
items.desc: Passenger’s Cusco partnership reflects a commitment to supporting coffee farming communities in Peru by fostering sustainably-focused growth and delivering exceptional, consistent coffees to customers year after year.

items.title: Keystone
items.desc: This dynamic blend of coffees from our Divino Niño and Agaro partnerships is roasted to highlight clear origin flavors that combine to create a uniquely delicious offering applicable to a wide array of brewing applications.

items.title: Necessary Colombia
items.desc: This classic Colombian profile delivers deeply satisfying candied nut and milk chocolate sweetness alongside subtle flavors of cooked red fruit.

items.title: Necessary Blend
items.desc: This enticing, easy-drinking blend of Colombian and Ethiopian coffees offers a harmonious balance of chocolate, brown sugar, and just a touch of fruit.

items.title: Agaro
items.desc: Showcasing the rich heritage of Ethiopian coffee, this offering is sourced in partnership with Addis Exporter, reflecting a steadfast commitment to quality and transparency in every cup.

完熟したチェリーを厳選し、24時間のPre-Fermentation(初期発酵)を行った後、果肉を除去し、糖分を豊富に含むミューシレージ(粘液質)のみを残します。その後、パッションフルーツと共に密閉タンク内で48時間のAnaerobic
Fermentationを実施。パッションフルーツ由来の成分と、コーヒーの糖分が相互に作用することで、複雑さとTropicalなフレーバーを引き出します。

items.desc:
GLITCH COFFEEだけのために選定された特別なカスタムロットが入荷しました。
Karamo Coffee、Ethiopian Coffee House、GLITCH COFFEEの3者によって実現した、オークションや通常販売を目的としない特別なロットです。
2020年 Ethiopia Cup of Excellence 初代チャンピオン、Nigusse Gemeda氏率いるKaramo Coffeeが、GLITCH COFFEEの理想とする味わいを追求し、少量のみ生産しました。

希少性だけでなく、明確なコンセプトのもとに生み出された、GLITCH COFFEEだけの特別な一杯です。

This Gesha selection, produced by Fabio Caballero Jr comes from his COE winning farm La Salvaje. His farm sits at 1820 MASL in a shaded forest where he grows Gesha, Pacamara, and SL-28. This Gesha lot was harvested form April-May 2025. This is our final release form Fabio this season and we are ending on a high note. This lot is very flavorful, with abundant fruits and bergamot florals. We are tasting raspberry, mango juice, strawberry and creamy florals.

items.title: Ethiopia | Keramo Adara
items.desc:
This coffee comes from the Keramo Adara Washing station, located at extreme elevations of up to 2350 MASL in the Bombe mountain range. About 1500 smallholder producers contribute their cherry to create this lot, with the primary variety being Heirloom 74112. The cup is bright and crisp with a pointed acidity and structured florality. We find notes of peach rings, limeade, pear, and elderflower.

items.title: Ethiopia | Idido
items.desc:
Idido is a remote community in Ethiopia's Yirgacheffe region. Here at 1900-2200 MASL local small holders deliver their cherry to be processed at the Idido washing station. This washed lot harvested in January 2025 is tasting balanced and sweet with notes of papaya, orange and lemon as well as black tea and vanilla.

items.title: Colombia | Luis & Robinson Cuellar
items.desc:
Luis Enrique Cuellar and his brother Robinson manage Finca La Pradera, a 6 hectare farm located at 2050 MASL in Santa Maria, Huila. They grow a range of varieties and this is a separation of Chiroso harvested in August 2025. This is a very juicy and fruit forward expression of Chiroso with notes of orange, blackberry, and tropical fruit like mango along with layered florals of elderflower

items.title: Ethiopia | Rumudamo
items.desc:
This coffee is sourced from the Rumudamo washing station in the village of Arbegona, located in Sidama. Harvested in January 2025 at an elevation of 2,200 MASL, around 600 local smallholder farmers contribute their cherries to create this lot. The primary variety delivered is Heirloom 74112. Expect a clean cup with a juicy acidity, sparkling florals and great complexity. We taste notes of lemon lime, nectarine, white peach, yuzu and jasmine.

items.title: Honduras | Danilo Sanchez
items.desc:
Danilo Sanchez is a coffee producer in El Paraíso, Honduras, just north of the Nicaraguan border. Here, at 1,500 MASL, he grows the Parainema variety on his farm, Los Cedros. This is our first year working with Danilo, after visiting him and his farm last March. This is also our first release of the Parainema variety. We taste a range of tropical, tart fruit flavors and florals. Up front we find bright raspberry, cooling into notes of cranberry, lime and mango with a herbal finish.

items.title: Colombia | Jhon Didier Trujillo
items.desc:
Jhon Didier Trujillo is a coffee producer in Urrao, Antioquia. His farm, Villa Flor sits at 1950 MASL, spanning 3.5 hectares. This small lot is a separation of Chiroso harvested in November 2025. We have tasted Jhon’s coffee many times, but this marks our first time purchasing his impressive Chiroso. We are finding big flavors, opening up to a cup with citrus, yellow fruits and light brown sugar. The cup cools into notes of orange creamsicle, elderflower and juicy mango.
Jhon is a passionate coffee farmer who has dedicated is life to coffee. He strives to be a role model for the younger genera

items.title: Honduras | Guillermo Tercero
items.desc:
Guillermo Tercero’s farm, El Tesoro spans 7 hectares within a lush forest along the Montecillos mountain range. This is a separation of his Pacamara, grown at 1750 MASL harvested in April, 2024. This is our first season working with Guillermo and we are thrilled to partner with him. His Pacamara is incredibly bright and juicy with notes of red fruits like pomegranate as well as apricot, a sugary sweetness and a spiced herbal note of rhubarb and spruce.
Visiting Guillermo’s farm is a breathtaking experience. Nestled within a forest, his coffee trees thrive in a healthy, shade-grown agroforestry

items.title: Decaf Colombia | Monkaaba
items.desc:
This decaffeinated lot is a collaboration of coffee producers within the Monkaaba network in San Agustin Colombia. Harvested in August 2025, the coffee comes from farms situated at altitudes between 1600 and 1900 MASL. It’s a sweetness-forward decaf with a soft pillowy mouthfeel with tasting notes of brown sugar, wafer cookie, and subtle hints of orange.

items.title: Primary Espresso | Guatemala
items.desc:
This iteration of our Primary Espresso comes from Jose Antonio Ramirez, a coffee producer in Las Tunas, San Miguel, Guatemala. This is a separation of Typica grown on his farm Rio Colorado at 1750 MASL, harvested in April 2026. Jose’s coffee is rich and flavorful with notes of tootsie roll, grape and plum as well as milk chocolate and almond cream.

items.title: Village Coffee and Goods Blend
items.desc:
We’ve partnered with Village Coffee & Goods to source an intentional, impactful coffee available for brew in-store and as a refillable option. This lot comes from core members of the Café Colis Resistencia in Mataquescuintla, Guatemala. It’s a field blend of Pache San Ramón, Catui, and Anacafé 14, grown at altitudes of 1700-1900 MASL. Chosen for its balance and approachability, this coffee appeals to both black coffee drinkers and those who prefer milk and sugar. Tasting notes include milk chocolate, nougat, and sweet plum and raisin.
This partnership with Village is about more than just great

items.title: Kenya — Gatomboya
items.desc:
Kenya — Gatomboya
Grown by smallholder farmers in Nyeri County, this fully washed lot brings together three Kenyan varieties: SL28, SL34 and Ruiru11. A classic expression of the region, expect a juicy cup with blackberry, subtle citrus acidity and fig leaf.
Following careful sorting, the cherries are pulped and fermented for 16-20 hours, depending on ambient temperatures, before being fully washed to remove the remaining mucilage. The parchment is then spread across raised drying beds, where it dries slowly over 12-20 days, with shade nets used during the hottest parts of the day.

items.title: DR Congo — Tumaini Coffee Co-Op
items.desc:
DR Congo — Tumaini Coffee Co-Op
The cherries are naturally processed and dried on raised beds at Tumaini’s collection centres, where access to running water can be limited. Assembly helped fund several of these drying beds during our first year working with the cooperative, allowing producers to dry their lots locally.
Drying the cherries whole helps retain their natural sweetness, resulting in a rich, rounded cup with a smooth finish.

items.title: Peru — Mikan
items.desc:
Peru — Mikan
Grown in the high-altitude areas around Jaén, this coffee benefits from a humid high-jungle climate, rich volcanic soils and plenty of tropical rainfall.
Ripe cherries are hand-picked and processed on the smallholder producers’ individual farms using hand-pulping machines, before being fermented in tanks and dried on patios or raised beds. Once processed all lots are sent to Falcon’s production facility, Mikan, in Jaén.
The washed process keeps things clean and balanced, highlighting the Tabi variety’s characteristic sweetness, citrus acidity and smooth body. Expect orange and van

items.title: Colombia — Cata Reserva Year 2
items.desc:
Colombia — Cata Reserva Year 2
Grown on a sunlit 4.5-acre plot of mature Castillo trees, this lot was selectively hand-sorted before processing.
Ripe cherries underwent 2–3 days of open-tank oxidation. The cherries were then pulped to remove the mucilage, before undergoing four days of sealed fermentation with coffee mosto – sugars from previous fermentations – and panela, an unrefined whole cane sugar.
This controlled approach encourages a thorough fermentation while avoiding unwanted alcohol-like flavours.

items.title: Colombia — Maria Rodriguez
items.desc:
Colombia — Maria Rodriguez
This SL28 is naturally processed, with a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation playing a key role in developing its depth of flavour.
Ripe cherries are harvested, floated and sorted before being placed in sealed tanks, where the controlled fermentation builds richer fruit character while retaining SL28’s signature clean profile. The cherries are then slowly sun-dried on raised beds for 20–30 days, turned regularly to ensure even dehydration and prevent over-fermentation.
The result is a distinctly tropical expression of SL28: ripe mango, butterscotch sweetness and a rounded

items.title: Rwanda — Jonathan Ngoga Year 2
items.desc:
Rwanda — Jonathan Ngoga Year 2
Cherries from Jonathan’s farm are processed as a dedicated single-producer lot at Muraho Trading Company’s Rugali washing station, alongside coffees from the surrounding smallholder community.
The cherries are hand-sorted before being floated and pulped, with underripe or damaged fruit removed at each stage. The coffee is then fermented for around 12 hours in concrete tanks, with the parchment agitated several times throughout the process. After fermentation, it is washed and graded by density before being hand-sorted again and laid out to dry for around 30 days.

Grown across La Esperanza’s network of farms, the coffee reflects the group’s long-standing commitment to exploring unusual varieties and refining the processes that bring out their potential.

items.title: Ecuador — La Rosita Sidra

Ecuador — La Rosita Sidra
Developed in Ecuador, Sidra is a locally adapted variety that combines an Ethiopian varietal with Ecuadorian terroir and growing conditions.
At La Rosita, the western foothills of the Andes provide a mild subtropical highland climate, where cool temperatures, frequent cloud cover and high annual rainfall encourage slow cherry maturation and greater sweetness.

items.desc:
Ecuador — La Rosita Bourbon
First cultivated on the island of Réunion before spreading across the coffee-growing world, Red Bourbon remains one of the industry's most revered varieties, celebrated for its natural sweetness and balance.
At La Rosita, the combination of cool Andean temperatures, humid cloud covered conditions and slow cherry maturation allows the variety to develop exceptional depth of flavour.

items.desc:
Ecuador — La Rosita Typica Mejorado
Situated on the western foothills of the Andes, La Rosita benefits from a mild subtropical highland climate, where cool temperatures, frequent cloud cover and high annual rainfall help to extend cherry maturation and develop greater sweetness and complexity. These same conditions, however, make drying coffee particularly challenging, particularly for honey and natural processes. For this reason, Rosa Morillo favours a washed approach.

items.title: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Kent
items.desc:
Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Kent
Selected at Doddengooda Estate in Mysore, India, Kent KP9293 was originally prized for its resistance to coffee leaf rust, while retaining the classic sweetness associated with the Typica varietal.
Whole cherries are pre-fermented for 24 hours beneath black tarpaulins to enhance sweetness and body before drying slowly in the sun over 25-26 days. Dried coffee is then transferred to hermetic storage until milling. The result is a silky smooth cup, full of ripe stone fruits and a boozy richness.

items.title: Guatemala — Santa Irene Catuaí
items.desc:
Guatemala — Santa Irene Catuaí
Catuaí is a cornerstone varietal of contemporary coffee production, prized for its resilience as much as its quality. While often associated with dependable everyday coffees, lots like this show just how expressive the variety can be when grown in exceptional conditions.
A classic washed process brings clarity and structure to the cup, revealing vibrant citrus, rounded sweetness and a lingering, syrupy finish.

items.title: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Geisha
items.desc:
Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Geisha
Although Geisha's route from Ethiopia to Central and South America passed through Tanzania, the varietal has remained largely absent from the country's coffee landscape. At Edelweiss, Neel and Kavita have reintroduced Geisha, sourcing and cultivating the seeds themselves to establish the variety on the estate.

items.title: Guatemala — Finca Gascón
items.desc:
Guatemala — Finca Gascón
This Catuai lot is processed as a natural, meaning the cherries are dried whole, with the fruit left intact around the seed. After harvest, the cherries are sorted, weighed and transported to the wet mill, before undergoing a 96-hour fermentation in GrainPro bags.
Felipe has refined this approach over the years, drawing from a broad set of processing protocols to produce coffees with structure and sweetness.
For this coffee, the result is a cup with vivid red fruit, subtle boozy notes and a sweet, rounded finish.

items.title: Colombia — Linarco Rodriguez Pink Bourbon
items.desc:
Colombia — Linarco Rodriguez Pink Bourbon
Pink Bourbon has become one of Colombia’s most sought-after varieties, prized for its clarity, floral aromatics and bright, structured acidity.
The lot underwent an open fermentation for around 48 hours at approximately 15°C. Once fermentation is complete, the coffee is washed and transferred to covered dryers where it dries slowly for 25 days at temperatures between 18–22°C. After drying, the coffee is packed and left to stabilise for a further 12 days.

items.title: Colombia — Linarco Rodriguez Castillo
items.desc:
Colombia — Linarco Rodriguez Castillo
This lot comes from producers across Huila, which are brought to Linarco’s farm for processing. The cherries are fermented between 14–22 °C for around 72 hours, before being pulped and left to oxidise for 48 hours.
The result is a beautifully structured washed profile. Sweetness and fruit clarity are complemented by a gentle creaminess and a lingering, balanced finish.

items.title: Mexico — Benancio Chavez
items.desc:
Mexico — Benancio Chavez
This lot is processed using a semi-washed (honey) method, where the coffee cherry is pulped but a layer of sticky mucilage is intentionally left on the parchment during drying.
After harvest, the cherries are rested intact for 24 hours, allowing the natural sugars to develop before pulping. Retaining this mucilage further enhances this lot's inherent sweetness. Drying takes place in Benancio’s solar dryer, where controlled conditions result in a cup that’s deliciously sweet and silky smooth.

items.title: Mexico — SIPRO
items.desc:
Mexico — SIPRO
This lot is naturally processed, where the coffee is dried whole in the cherry after harvest. With the fruit left intact, sugars are absorbed back into the seed as it dries, building depth and intensity of flavour.
The result is a cup full of fruit-forward sweetness, with notes of dried fruit and a dense, syrupy texture. This is the fourth year in a row we’ve shared this coffee with you and once again, it’s a real standout.

Pacamara is prized for its intensity and complexity – combining floral aromatics with a bright, citrus fruit acidity that gives the cup a distinctive taste.
This lot is processed as a semi-washed (honey), where some mucilage is left intact after pulping before undergoing 48 hours of controlled fermentation. During this stage, oxidation builds on the varietal’s inherent qualities, giving additional sweetness.

items.title: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Mielado
items.desc:
Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Mielado
Bourbon N39 is a Tanzanian Bourbon, first developed in the 1930s for quality and yield.
This lot underwent an extended, high-temperature fermentation. Cherries were held for six days in a controlled, exothermic environment, where elevated temperatures drove the development of complex, fruit-forward esters while reinforcing the variety’s natural sweetness and structure. Following fermentation, the cherries were pulped, leaving a measured amount of mucilage intact.
The result is a velvety, smooth cup with stone fruit sweetness and a slight nuttiness.

Once harvested the Cata Pacamara was fermented in cherry (the beans still encased in their mucilage) for close to five days. The mucilage was then removed from the beans before another 24-hour fermentation and a final wash to finish the process.

To achieve these qualities with the Assembly House Espresso, we source coffees that naturally exhibit these characteristics. And then we roast them in ways that ensure they are fully optimised for espresso and also offer a delicious cup when brewed with all other methods - especially French Press.

items.desc: Fruit Cake is a little slice of holiday comfort. Juicy pineapple and golden raisin bring a rich, fruit-forward sweetness, while chocolate caramels melt into a smooth, indulgent finish. A festive cup that feels right at home alongside your favourite holiday treats.

black plum / chocolate truffle / dates / brandy

items.title: Second Slice / Costa Rica
items.desc: Second Slice is pure comfort in a cup. Warm cinnamon and baked apple pie bring the sweetness, while toasted pecan adds a rich, nutty finish. A cozy Costa Rican coffee that tastes like going back for another piece.

items.title: Sundae Drive / Papua New Guinea
items.desc: Sundae Drive is a sweet little escape to the lush highlands of Papua New Guinea. Creamy vanilla and rich caramel melt into warm, toasty pecan, creating a comforting cup that feels like dessert without ever being too much.

items.title: Favourite Pear / Burundi
items.desc: Favourite Pear is soft, elegant, and quietly comforting. Juicy pear sweetness drifts through delicate notes of Earl Grey, while a smooth touch of vanilla rounds out the cup with warmth and grace. This Burundi coffee feels familiar from the very first sip—gentle, refined, and easy to fall in love with.

items.title: Full Bloom / Colombia
items.desc: Full Bloom bursts open with vibrant hibiscus florals and the bright sparkle of clementine, balanced by a soft almond sweetness that lingers gently on the finish. Delicate yet expressive, it’s a cup that captures the feeling of spring at its peak—colourful, lively, and full of possibility.

items.title: Jam Jar / Ethiopia
items.desc: Jam Jar is bursting with the kind of sweetness that keeps you coming back for more. Juicy blueberry jam meets rich chocolate and a drizzle of buttery toffee, creating a cozy, indulgent cup with all the charm of a homemade treat. A little sweetness worth savouring, straight from Ethiopia.

blood orange / jasmine / strawberry / mandarin orange / creamy

items.title: Cherry Wild / Colombia

untamed. Bursting with ripe cherry brightness, the cup carries the rich, spiced depth of fruitcake, lifted by a sparkling hint of tangerine.

items.title: Hanan Million Natural | Guji, Ethiopia
items.desc:
Local landrace varieties carrying the particular character of Buku Hambella. Hanan founded ASHKIM with her mother, Asha Yuya, the name honouring Asha and her sister Kimiya.
The fermentation that happens inside a drying coffee fruit is microbially complex and environmentally responsive, and the difference between a natural that sings and one that doesn't comes down to decisions made on the drying bed across weeks. Hanan's lands in the expressive register: purple haribo gummies, bubblegum, white tea are things we’ve been picking up with this one.

items.title: Moata Raya Lunar Honey | Agaro, Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot is a fun experiment using 74110 local landrace (and catalogued by JARC) grown by smallholder farmers on garden plots in Agaro. Moata bought this fruit from locals as he doesn't have a farm, but he still wanted to work through this processing idea - and we get to enjoy the results together. This lot is a honey, where Moata used a hand disk pulper with no further soak, and laid the parchment out on raised beds, covered with shade mesh during the day, and opening the netting at dusk and overnight, resulting in things like nougaty white mulberry, taffy and oolong.

items.title: Basha Bekele Natural (minis) | Sidama, Ethiopia
items.desc: Variety 74158 grown by 1st place COE winner (2024), Basha Bekele, on his farm in Bombe, Bensa, Sidama. Proccessed as a natural with whole fruit dried on raised beds. This lot is particularily special as it features the smallest screen sizes, not normally exportable. Moata, who works with Crop to Cup took it upon himself to painstakingly re-sort these 'minis', with the idea that these smaller fruits have outsized flavour. We're inclined to agree.

items.desc:
Kai and Jannette Janson are the main people behind Janson Family Estates - and are two of the loveliest people in Panama. They've been running the operations at the farm, located in the town of Volcan, for many years now - preceded by generations in the Janson family.

items.title: Danche Hydro Honey
items.desc: We're welcoming in a new lot that we haven't worked with this producer before, and we've got to say - it's something very special! This is from the Danche Washing Station, in Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, very closely located to the Chelbesa stations. The cherry here is sourced from 810 registered growers in the villages Danche and Kubi, in Gedeo zone, Gedeb. The average elevation of the farms lies at around 2100 Meters Above Sea level on rich and fertile red soil in a semi-forested environment, and harvest takes place between November and January. Cherry variety is Mixed Heirloom / Ethiopian Land Ra

items.title: Kiandu AA Washed
items.desc:
Great, classic washed Kenyan coffees are getting harder and harder to find unfortunately. Subtle changes to farming practices, environmental reasons, and changes to varieties mean that the classic Kenyan profile of old is much more rare. This Kiandu AA lot is a great representation of how great and fruity Kenyan Washed coffees can be!

items.title: Bambito Estate Geisha Washed (Competition Lot)
items.desc:
Ever since first trying Ivan and Priscilla's coffee's in 2022, we loved what they produced. Their elusive Washed Geisha is a rare lot that speaks for itself in quality and elegance - something super special, and worth appreciating!
Grown in Bambito, nearby Volcan in Panama (just off the road leading to Cerro Punta), the land where their geisha grows goes up the mountain to around 1800m above sea level. items.title: Alo Main Station Dark Room Dry Natural
items.desc:
From the main station of Alo Village, and a producer we've worked with for several years now, comes a very special lot that represents how much Tamiru Tadesse has pushed processing at Alo. This lot is a classic natural, without extra fermentation but has a special dark room drying. Tamiru built these dark rooms for drying coffee a few years ago, but has expanded them recently to accomodate more lots, and we were lucky enough to get this one, lot #34. This whole 17kg lot has been sent to us, and we're happy to share it with you now.

items.title: Mama Sierra Caturra Washed
items.desc:
This is your answer to a daily coffee that's good on price, giving a dependable flavour profile, and enjoyable every day without being too much. Mama Sierra, led by Sirley Pulgarin of The Coffee Quest Colombia, is a remarkable project empowering women coffee farmers in the community of Giraldo, Antioquia. With 15 motivated members, the project began in March 2021, initiated by Yessica Parra and later taken forward by Sirley. The goal has always been to break barriers limiting women’s access to resources and training in coffee production.

items.title: Kotowa Las Brujas Geisha Clean Natural
items.desc:
This year is the first year we're buying from Kotowa Farms in Boquete, and we're absolutely thrilled to offer this amazing Geisha from their Las Brujas farm lot 26-094!
This lot in particular is their outstanding Geisha, which was processed with a "Natural" process, although the result in the cup is something that reminds us much more of a washed. We had confirmed with the farm that it was infact a natural, even though it does appear more washed. items.title: Chilaka Anaerobic Natural
items.desc:
Tamiru Tadesse is a coffee supplier who has been in the coffee business for the last eight years. He works with about 200 farmers in Delo Kebele, Bensa zone of the Sidama region. He collects about 182,000 kilograms of red cherry from an estimated 80 hectares of land owned by the farmers. Tamiru processes anaerobic and natural coffee which is dried on a raised bed with mesh wire. He then sells his coffee on the international market, mostly in China. However, he says, he was interested to have new market destinations and promote the unique flavours of Bensa coffee.

items.title: Altieri Pre-dry Natural Geisha DFM
items.desc:
This is our first year visiting and buying from the Altieri farm in Boquete, and it was an absolute treat. Getting to see their facilities, and cup their outstanding lots from a variety of processes and elevations is really impressive! We purchased a few lots from them, and the first to be released is this pre-dry natural Geisha.
This lot is from their Tom lot - it sits around 1700m above sea level at Alto Quiel, in Boquete, Panama. It covers an area of approximately 1 hectare of volcanic soil where Geisha Green Tip grows. It is adjacent to the protected area of the Volcan Baru national park,

items.title: Guji Rassa Washed
items.desc:
This is a classic washed Ethiopian coffee that ticks all the boxes. You can imagine that when someone says "washed Ethiopian coffee" you have a profile in mind - this is exactly that - nothing more, nothing less.
Grown from 2000-2200masl in the village of Rassa, in the Guji region of Ethiopia, this lot is comprised of mixed heirloom varieties without specific selection of varieties that comes with several smallholder farmers producing cherries at a time. The cherries are sent to the Suke Washing station where they're processed in the traditional washed fashion - floated, depulped, washed, and

items.title: Chiroso Washed Las Perlitas
items.desc:
A washed Chiroso from Las Perlitas in Antioquia, Colombia, sourced through Coffee Quest. Smallholder deliveries are cupped separately and combined when their profiles complement one another.
Bright, juicy and sweet, with orange, prune and almond in the cup. We roast it to work beautifully as both filter and espresso.

items.title: Cherry Ripe Blend
items.desc:
This coffee is born out of a simple question - how can we make an espresso blend that's the most fruity as possible, while still being clear and clean. We have been working on this lot for several months, starting right from sourcing. We worked hand in hand with our friends at Cofinet to source these components and design this blend around 3 particular lots.
Firstly a Washed and Natural Caturra - these set the base for our blend providing a fruity, yet well structured base. The last component is a small amount of a Cherry co-fermented coffee from Jairo Arcilla. This is what gives us that big b

items.title: Rose Rejects
items.desc:
Rose Rejects is coffee that didn’t make it into our main lineup.
It’s a mix of beans rejected by our colour sorter — including quakers and beans that are visually over-roasted — alongside roasted batches that missed our internal targets by being too light, too dark, or otherwise outside spec. Nothing unsafe, nothing adulterated, just coffee that didn’t meet the standard we set for Rose.
This is not a curated blend and it’s not meant to be expressive or particularly tasty. Expect a very basic cup. Sometimes flat, sometimes rough, sometimes fine — but never special. If you’re looking for clarity

items.title: The House Blend
items.desc:
This is a special "House Blend" that we've designed specifically for use on Espresso machines / Bialetti. It's an easy drinking coffee that has a well developed roast profile to make it easy to extract, while still keeping recognisable flavours of the origins. We would call this a "Medium - Dark" roast. Not so much that the beans are all oily, but developed enough to have Low Acidity, Smooth Body, and mostly chocolatey flavour notes.
All the coffees we use in this are Specialty coffee, but with very approachable taste profiles and qualities. We've sourced these lots either direct from farmers,

items.title: The Bedtime Blend
items.desc:
This is a blend that we've designed especially to be as delicious as non-decaffeinated coffee - to be used for Espresso/Bialetti brewing and goes amazing as both a black coffee, and with milk.
We believe that decaffeinated coffee doesn't have to come at the sacrifice of quality - so we created this Decaf blend that is as delicious as full strength coffee. Generally you will find more sweetness and acidity, as the balance with the bitter caffeine has been removed. In some of these coffees we find more spice, and malt notes from the decaf process, and some darker roasted notes from the darker ro

items.title: Jingle Beans Holiday Blend
items.desc: Behold! A coffee is born. 'Tis the freaking season and what have you! Oh, Jingle Beans, oh Jingle Beans, our annual ho-li-day blend. Each year we go out of our way to make this blend as seasonally outlandish as we can. This year, two coffees from Ethiopia — a washed and a naturally processed — triumphantly coalesce into the best interpretation of drinkable fruit cake in a cup. Jingle Beans, Jingle Beans, Jingle all the beans.

items.title: David Muñoz - Honduras
items.desc: For the second consecutive year, we kick off Honduran season with a coffee from David Muñoz, a producer who’s been a mainstay on the Tandem menu for a decade. David grows multiple varieties on his roughly 3 hectare farm, Nueva Esperanza, in Santa Barbara, but the majority is Pacas. This 100% Pacas lot is soft and sweetness-driven. We taste a familiar, balanced cup with flavors of caramel, milk chocolate, toasted nuts, and gentle plum-like acidity.

items.title: Arley Arboleda - Colombia
items.desc: This small lot from Arley Arboleda is another excellent Chiroso from Urrao. Arley is a 36-year-old, second-generation producer growing Chiroso at 2,100 masl across two hectares. He learned coffee farming from his father as a teenager and purchased the land for Finca Los Guaicos in 2022 with the specific goal of cultivating exclusively Chiroso. As with many producers in the region, Arley uses the cochadas method, a regional processing practice in which each day’s harvest is depulped and added to the same fermentation tank throughout the week. Once the tank is full, the coffee is washed together

items.title: Chelbesa - Ethiopia
items.desc: We’re excited to have back on our menu for another season this bright, refreshing classic from the Chelbesa One Washing Station. Approximately 1,000 smallholder farmers deliver cherry to Chelbesa One, one of seven washing stations across Ethiopia managed by SNAP Coffee. Cherries are sorted, floated, and depulped, then dry fermented in tanks for 48-72 hours before being washed and placed to dry on raised beds for 7-10 days. Coffees from this station are typically pristine and elegant. Expect a crisp, lightly effervescent profile with white tea aromatics and flavors of grapefruit, melon, and pea

items.title: Kibingo - Kenya
items.desc: This washed field blend from Kibingo Estate is another stellar coffee sourced via Kamavindi Coffee Labs. Established in 1957 with just 100 trees — the maximum allotment for Kenyan growers under colonial law at the time — Kibingo has since grown into one of the country’s most highly regarded estate farms. The estate won Kenya’s Taste of Harvest competition in 2024, and owner Anthony Kimani has continued investing in farm-level and processing infrastructure, with plans to expand beyond its current 6,000 trees. In the cup, we taste ripe red fruits like pomegranate and raspberry, sweet spice, and

items.title: Oneska - Kenya
items.desc: Oneska is the small estate farm of Onesmus Njagi, a retired schoolteacher, and his wife, Karen, on the slopes of Mount Kenya in Embu County. Last fall, we visited ahead of harvest and toured their four hectares, where they grow the traditional SL-28 and SL-34 varieties at good altitude and under ideal growing conditions. The name Oneska is a portmanteau of Onesmus and Karen, who established the farm in the early 1990s and have spent decades honing their agronomic and processing practices. items.title: Heri Agena - Ethiopia
items.desc: This microlot is the first of four coffees we’ll feature this year from Karamo Coffee, a quality-driven export company working in the high-altitude regions of Bensa and Bura in Sidama. We met Teddy of Karamo in Addis Ababa last year for a quick cupping and were very impressed by the quality of the coffees on the table. items.title: Danche Yellow Honey- Ethiopia
items.desc: This honey-processed Ethiopian coffee comes to us from Danche station in Gedeb, one of two sites operated by SNAP Specialty Coffee in the kebele of Chelbesa. Founded in 2019, Danche now processes cherry from approximately 800 nearby smallholder farmers, most of whom grow small amounts of coffee on 2-3 hectare plots of land at significant elevation. Danche began with a focus on washed lots but has since expanded to include natural, honey, and experimental preparations. items.title: Alma Pineda - Cup of Excellence - Honduras
items.desc: This year, we purchased a split share of Alma Pineda’s washed Gesha lot, one of our top-scoring coffees from the 2026 Honduras Cup of Excellence (CoE). Alma’s coffees have placed at the Honduras CoE before, including third in 2019 and second in 2024, with this lot placing eighth in the Exotic Varieties category. Her farm, El Limo, sits at 1650 masl in Santa Barbara, where nearly all the Honduran coffee on our menu is grown. Alma received the land from her father in 2012, and after a year working abroad to save money, she returned home to invest in her farms and coffees. Her Gesha is a stellar

items.title: Faver Ninco - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first of three Pink Bourbon lots we’ll be featuring from the main harvest at Finca Costa Rica, Faver Ninco’s 10-hectare farm in Santa Maria. At just over 2,000 masl, Finca Costa Rica experiences cooler temperatures than much of the region, with more limited sunlight and less regular rainfall. These factors combine to produce more sporadic flowering and nearly year-round picking. Within that fluid cycle, Finca Costa Rica still has a defined main harvest season that runs from May to August, with this first lot coming from the early and peak portions of the harvest.
